name: Machine-context audit: detect fabricated or slanted in-product AI summaries and test the retail drift they cause
one_line: Continuously fact-check Polymarket's own AI 'Market Context' timelines, and where they cite non-existent or mislabelled sources in a directional way, test for and fade the retail flow that reads them.
scope: Collect context entries for markets of $1M and above. An agent checks that each citation resolves to a real article from the claimed outlet. Sign each error by the outcome it favours. Run an event study of price and small-ticket flow after the entry appears. The defensive use is to block the team's own agents from ingesting platform context. A sub-variant is a poisoned-source sentinel for the LLM-bot herd, since a Pravda-network domain was cited 1,000+ times per the E7 pack. The decisive unknown is whether these errors move prices at all. The first step is pure logging over 8-12 weeks.
why_it_matters: The E7 pack lists this fact and no entry monetises it or defends against it. The CJR audit covered 152 markets with at least $1M at stake and 65,000+ entries. Nearly a third of annotated markets carried fake AP URLs, concentrated in election markets. The examples were directional, including a fake AOC announcement and a Harris-Iran deal attributed to the FT that linked to a pro-Russian network. Polymarket did not respond. Every retail user on the page sees this common-mode input. I recommend folding it into llm-monoculture-herd-factor, renamed 'predictable-herd factor', as the 'machine-generated context' sub-variant, not giving it a separate file.
flags: The ToS bans scraping the site with robots or crawlers (E9 pack). Never create or seed content. Trading against a known platform defect while it goes unreported is an optics risk.

key_evidence.note: Columbia Journalism Review, 2026-08-27. The audit covered 152 markets at $1M and above and 65,000+ entries. Nearly a third had fabricated AP links. The search vendor was Linkup. Polymarket did not respond.

critic_notes: RENAME llm-monoculture-herd-factor to 'predictable-herd factor' and add three sub-variants. (a) Copy-cascade harvesting: follower flow is labelled on-chain by builder code (PolyCop and Polygun fills; median copy delay 5.6 min, p90 9.6; E6 pack). A leader fill therefore predicts follower takers minutes later. Note the collapse to about $28.5M a month of copy-bot volume in Aug 2026 (E6 pack), which makes capacity small. (b) Machine-context audit (see missing: platform-ai-context-audit). (c) Poisoned-source sentinel. Trading ahead of your own followers is prohibited. Providing liquidity to strangers' public copy flow is not.
